evidence: The finding's premise (ReplicaRouter can route ReviewUserSettings.load() to a lagging replica) does not hold in this tree. ReviewUserSettings.load (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:310-314) reads via cls.objects.for_team(team_id).filter(user_id=...).first(); TeamScopedManager.for_team (posthog/models/scoping/manager.py:118-131) builds the queryset with using=self._db, which is unset, so the DATABASE_ROUTERS chain decides. That chain (posthog/settings/data_stores.py:119-127, 261-262) is ProductDBRouter (only when product DBs are configured) then ReplicaRouter (only when POSTHOG_POSTGRES_READ_HOST is set). ProductDBRouter.db_for_read (posthog/product_db_router.py:27-35) returns a _db_reader alias only for app labels in products/db_routing.yaml:2-9 (stamphog, visual_review, warehouse_sources_queue, agent_platform); review_hog is not routed, so it returns None. ReplicaRouter.db_for_read (posthog/dbrouter.py:22-31) returns 'replica' only when the env list READ_REPLICA_OPT_IN (data_stores.py:271-272) contains 'ALL_MODELS_USE_READ_REPLICA' or the literal class name 'ReviewUserSettings'; the only opt-in names referenced anywhere in the tree are 'local_evaluation' (products/feature_flags/backend/local_evaluation.py:384) and 'decide' (posthog/database_healthcheck.py:10). Default routing therefore sends both gate reads (receivers.py:114 and :154, plus the resolve-snapshot read at temporal/activities.py:600) to 'default', i.e. the writer, and the suggested .using(router.db_for_write(ReviewUserSettings)) would also resolve to 'default' (dbrouter.py:33-37) - a no-op. The writer pins the finding copies (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:295-300, temporal/activities.py:103 etc.) exist because stamphog models live on a separate product DB with a real reader endpoint; that reasoning does not transfer to a main-DB model. Even under a hypothetical ops opt-in, the ReplicaRouter docstring bounds lag at <100ms (dbrouter.py:17-19), and the queued stamphog initial review already trusts the toggle resolved at dispatch without any recheck (tasks.py:1110-1116; cluster precedent W12 'Queued initial reviews ignore toggle changes before execution' judged not real), so a sub-100ms stale read at the receiver adds nothing to the by-design trust-at-dispatch window and is not a security boundary. Cluster note: LA22 is the same claim as cluster 76 member E3 (ReviewUserSettings toggle gates need writer pinning; 0/1 real in July), not the same as W10 - W10 targeted find_task_run in the tasks facade (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py) returning None under lag and permanently suppressing re-reviews; the two share only the false premise that main-DB reads hit a replica by default.
notes: Would flip to real (should_fix at most, not must_fix) if the tree opted ReviewUserSettings into the read replica (READ_REPLICA_OPT_IN listing it or ALL_MODELS_USE_READ_REPLICA, or a db_routing.yaml route for review_hog with a reader alias) AND the queued stamphog task rechecked the toggle so that a stale read at the receiver were the only remaining window. Ops env config outside the tree cannot be verified here; if prod sets READ_REPLICA_OPT_IN=ALL_MODELS_USE_READ_REPLICA the read would go to the replica, but the consequence is bounded by <100ms lag and by the existing dispatch-time trust, so severity would be consider.
